findings.title: Ruby method redefinition breaks emoji resizing
findings.description: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: the new dimensions-based `downsize` replaces the preceding width/height definition. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb`, which now raises `ArgumentError` because five arguments are passed to a method accepting three or four. Preserve both calling conventions through argument normalization, or give the dimensions-based method a distinct name. Add regression coverage for both forms.

findings.title: Fixed browser limit incorrectly applies to attachments
findings.description: Replacing the type-specific setting with 10 MB changes attachment validation even though only images gain automatic downsizing. Sites configured to accept attachments larger than 10 MB now have valid uploads blocked in the browser. Conversely, attachments exceeding a smaller configured limit pass browser validation only to be rejected by `Validators::UploadValidator`. Retain `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments and apply the larger incoming-image allowance only to images.

findings.title: Existing size-validation test contradicts the new behavior
findings.description: The existing “prevents files that are too big from being uploaded” test sets a 5 KB image limit and expects a 10 KB image to fail validation. The changed implementation accepts it and does not show the expected alert, so these assertions no longer match the intended contract. Update this test to exercise the incoming-image limit, retain coverage for configured attachment limits, and add controller coverage for successful downsizing and conversion failure. The inspected controller specs do not exercise the new retry loop.
